summary: SCOPE: the rounds:M4.43 cap argument in baselines/review.txt only, per the round-7 brief -- the three questions asked, nothing else. No code and no tests are staged, so there is no mutation to survive; the mutation matrix and the backlog rows are carried forward from earlier rounds and I did NOT re-verify TR-M4.43-1 or the M4.41 remedy this round. (1) TR-M4.43-3 IS CLOSED, and I checked it against the artefacts rather than the prose: the self-correction is exact. TR-M4.17-6 (3893ebde..., test-reviewer, 05:22) reads 'the class alone green 5/5 on an idle machine with instrumented values fastRate=3 slowRate=0 every run' and proposes 'raise the floor from 3 to 4' -- the entry's 'proposed the floor of 4 from five runs all reading fastRate=3' is verbatim. TR-M4.17-3 (e8a3151c..., test-reviewer, 05:38) reads 'fastRate = 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 over five class-scoped runs ... plus two full :sequencer:test runs (246 tests)' and 'THE FLOOR OF 4 DOES NOT KILL multipliedBy(2)' -- 'withdrew it from seven runs reading 4,3,4,4,3 plus two module-wide' is exact, and the seven decomposes the same way in both places it appears in the entry (5 class + 2 module), so the two mentions cannot be read as fourteen runs. (2) NOTHING NOW CREDITS EITHER ROLE WITH THE OTHER'S WORK. 'THE TEST REVIEWER measured ... 3 of 7 runs (~43%), bimodal at 3/4, honest never below 6 including at load average 123' is TR-M4.17-3 verbatim. 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently, recording fast=6, 7, 7 for the 2x mutant at a 2000ms window' is M4.43-R1d (68c71440...reviewer.json) verbatim -- production's own tree, its own three runs. The disagreement clause is supported at both ends: e8a3151c.test-reviewer.json is timestamped 05:38 and says 'kills it about 40% of the time'; e8a3151c.reviewer.json is timestamped 05:40 and its summary says 'the floor keeps 1.75x slack'. Note the 1.75x figure ORIGINATES in TR-M4.17-6's own remedy, but the entry only says the production verdict says it, which is true, so this is not a credit transfer. 'stands uncorrected' is supported by production's own later audit (57281fcd, d7b93c2c). The M0.64 citation added in this delta is exact -- backlog.md:33 headlines 'A REVIEWER CAN REPORT A VERDICT IT NEVER RECORDED' and the row is todo, so 'already files the general case' holds. (3) REMOVING 'the final round passed both roles' IS AN IMPROVEMENT, not a loss, and I withdraw the do-not-fix half of TR-M4.43-4 on that specific clause: the claim was unverifiable at the moment it was written, since the round it described had no verdict yet, and three further rounds then falsified it -- a permanent file asserting a round outcome it could not know is the non-negotiable-4 shape, not merely a stale ordinal. Nothing load-bearing went with it: the substance (two last findings, introduced by the fix before them, both the same counting shape, recorded rather than chased) survives intact, and 'an earlier draft of this line proved it again' is itself true and checkable. One minor came in with the replacement justification, recorded and NOT recommended for fixing -- see TR-M4.43-5.

findings.summary: The clause that replaced the removed round outcome cites rounds:M4.7a for a broader rule than M4.7a states, and M4.7a visibly does the thing the broader rule forbids. New text: 'THIS ENTRY CLAIMS NO CONVERGENCE, and states no round outcome, because a ROUND FACT carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it -- rounds:M4.7a in this file says so'. baselines/review.txt:13 actually says 'the COUNT is left to review_rounds.py, because a COUNT carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it' -- and then narrates round facts by hand for four rounds, ending 'Round 4: passed both roles clean, no findings', which is a round OUTCOME stated in prose. rounds:M4.17 and rounds:M4.38 do the same. So M4.7a supports the narrow rule (a COUNT, and by the same rationale a TERMINAL claim like 'the final round', because neither is knowable when the sentence is written) and contradicts the broad one as generalised.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15 (M4's VERIFIED.md and milestone review) is the next open row and reads baselines/review.txt end to end. It reaches the M4.43 citation, follows it to line 13, and finds M4.7a stating per-round findings and a round outcome by hand -- so either M4.7a breaks a rule the file attributes to it, or M4.43 misread it, and nothing in either entry says which. The second-order cost is worse than the confusion: applied as written, the generalisation deletes the per-round narration in M4.7a, M4.17 and M4.38 that is the only reason those cap arguments are auditable, when what the record supports is the narrow and useful rule that an entry cannot state its OWN round's outcome. This is the same defect class the entry itself is about -- citing an artefact for a claim the artefact does not make, which is TR-M4.17-9 against M4.40 and M4.17-R3b against the same row. ⚠️ RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: commit body, NOT a fix. It is one word ('round fact' for 'count') in a sentence whose conclusion is correct, the entry's own last line records that fixing minors here produced the last two rounds' findings, and a fix rewrites the exact clause round 7 exists to have settled. I raised the previous ordinal minor as do-not-fix, it was fixed, and this finding is the surface that fix created -- which is itself the argument.
